### [19] [Large Language Models without QK-Normalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10560)
*Yongding Tao,Yitong Qiao,Tianqi Shao,Tian Wang,Zhixuan Chu,Xiaoming Wu,Yihong Dong,Ge Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出 QK-MAP（Magnitude-Aware Projection），用学习的周期性（多频率 sin/cos）特征替代 QK-Norm，把"输入幅度"信息从向量长度迁移到相位与坐标模式上：特征范数恒定（‖Φ(x)‖²=m）且对幅度保持可微敏感，从而在控制注意力 logit 增长的同时保留 token 级幅度信息。在 190M–7B 的严格匹配预训练实验中，QK-MAP 在所有规模上取得最低训练/验证交叉熵，并在 7B 上取得最佳 Avg-8 下游准确率；分析显示其对输入尺度仍敏感、注意力更少集中在首 token（attention sink 减弱）、在合成长上下文任务中对相关证据的注意力对比更强。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: QK-Norm（QK-RMSNorm / QK-L2Norm）被 OLMo 3、Qwen 3 等现代大模型广泛用于抑制 query/key 范数增长、防止 attention logit 爆炸与 softmax 饱和。但作者指出范数不仅是不稳定源，还承载 token 级信息：把 q_i = r_i u_i、k_j = r_j v_j 代入 logit 可知，query 范数 r_i^q 缩放整行 logit，等效于 query 依赖的逆温度（控制注意力分布尖锐度），key 范数 r_j^k 缩放整列 logit，决定某 token 被不同 query 关注的强度。ℓ2/RMSNorm 对正比例缩放完全不变（Proposition 1：ε=0 时 N_0(ru)=N_0(u)，ε>0 时径向敏感度按 O(r^-3) 衰减；learned gain 跨 token 共享也无法恢复逐 token 的幅度信号），因此归一化在"控制尺度"与"保留幅度信息"之间存在权衡。核心问题即：能否控制 query-key 表示而不丢失对幅度的敏感性？

Method: 方法：QK-MAP（Magnitude-Aware Projection）用学习的周期表示替换归一化。先由可学习 W_p ∈ R^{D×m}、b_p 计算 Φ(x) = [cos(xW_p + b_p); sin(xW_p + b_p)] ∈ R^{2m}（主配置 m = D/2，故输出维数与输入同维；Q/K 共享同一 Φ，但各自独立的 W_Q、W_K；value 路径不变，投影后 reshape heads 并照常加 RoPE）。随后给出三条理论性质：Proposition A.2——‖Φ(x)‖² = m 恒定，J_Φ^T J_Φ = W_p W_p^T，因此 ‖∂Φ(ru)/∂r‖ = ‖W_p^T u‖ 不随 r 衰减（幅度敏感性不随幅度消失）；Proposition A.3——logit 界 |s_ij| ≤ (m/√d_h)‖A_Q‖_op‖A_K‖_op 与 ‖x‖ 无关（幅度无关的有界 logit）；Proposition A.4/A.5——多频率使 r ↦ Φ(ru) 在 r 上几乎处处单射，且在任意有限幅度区间上满足正的分离下界（消除单频率的周期性歧义）。默认实现加入逐维可学习残差 Ψ_α(x) = Φ(x) + Diag(α)x（α 零初始化），配合前置 RMSNorm 保证有界。跨尺度实验使用参数匹配的残差版本 QK-MAP-R（略微缩减 FFN 宽度以对齐参数量，差异 ≤0.033%）。对比方法包括 Standard attention、QK-Norm、QK-Clip（Kimi K2 的 logit 裁剪）与 QUEST（仅归一化 key，保留 query 温度）。

Result: 主要结果：(1) 语言建模——QK-MAP 在 190M/370M/760M/1B/7B 五个规模上训练与验证 CE 均为最低（7B：train 2.23、val 2.86，对比 QK-Norm 2.24/2.90、Standard 2.25/2.89）；验证改进在 C4、Pile、M2D2-S2ORC 与六个 Dolma 域上一致。7B 的 Avg-8 = 56.75 为最佳（QK-Norm 55.48、Standard 55.86），且在末段 16 个共同检查点上全部排名第一（对 Standard 平均领先 0.45 个百分点）。(2) 幅度信息使用——190M 上跨序列打乱 key 范数使 CE 上升 0.194（QK-MAP）与 0.188（Standard），而 QK-Norm 仅 0.00012，证明 QK-MAP 与 Standard 一样真正使用 token 级 key 幅度；按 head 分别打乱时 QK-Norm 仍敏感（0.628），QK-MAP 更低（0.330）。(3) 注意力分配——QK-MAP 首 token 注意力（F-Attn）在 55 个"域×长度"格子中全部低于两个基线，11 域均值比 Standard 低 9.1%–12.7%；合成证据 SNR 在所有长度上最高，相对 QK-Norm 的增益从 32 token 的 24.9% 增至 600 token 的 85.3%，并在 1/2/3 needle 与多任务提示上均成立。(4) 文本扰动——190M WikiText-103 词替换测试中，QK-MAP 在干净文本与 1.5%/2.5%/5% 替换率下困惑度均最低（5% 时比 QK-Norm 低 13.8%、比 QUEST 低 16.8%）。(5) 消融——QK-MAP-D / -P / -R 三种集成方式（直连映射、无残差、参数匹配残差）在各规模至少一种优于两个基线，说明收益不依赖单一集成规则。

Conclusion: 结论：QK-Norm 在抑制 attention logit 增长的同时抹去了 query/key 承载的大量 token 级幅度信息；QK-MAP 通过学习的多频率周期特征，将幅度信息编码进相位与坐标模式而非仅依赖向量长度，实现"尺度可控 + 幅度敏感"的解耦。190M–7B 的一致语言建模收益、更低的首 token 注意力（缓解 attention sink）与更强的相关证据注意力对比，说明 query-key 尺度控制不必以牺牲幅度信息为代价，QK-MAP 可作为 QK 归一化的实用替代。局限与边界：多频率单射性依赖频率比非有理等充分条件（学习过程中可能改变频率，故仅为充分条件）；幅度区分仍存在周期性歧义；分析基于合成提示与 190M/7B 探针，残差变体使范数界依赖输入归一化域（‖Ψ_α(x)‖ ≤ √m + ‖α‖_∞ B）；跨尺度参数匹配通过缩减 FFN 宽度实现。

Abstract: Query-Key Normalization (QK-Norm) is widely adopted in modern large language models to control the growth of attention logits and improve training stability. However, query and key norms are not merely sources of instability. The query norm controls the sharpness of the attention distribution, while the key norm determines how strongly a token attracts different queries. These norms therefore carry token-specific information about attention selectivity and token importance. By normalizing both, QK-Norm suppresses this information. This raises a natural question: can we control query-key representations without discarding their sensitivity to magnitude? To address this question, we propose QK-MAP, a Magnitude-Aware Projection for constructing queries and keys. Rather than removing magnitude through normalization, QK-MAP transforms the input representation using multiple learnable frequencies, so that changes in magnitude are encoded as bounded phase patterns. This allows magnitude to be represented through phase and direction rather than vector length alone. Its periodic features have a fixed norm while remaining sensitive to magnitude changes, separating magnitude encoding from norm growth. Multiple frequencies further help distinguish magnitudes and reduce periodic ambiguity. Experiments across model scales from 190M to 7B parameters show that QK-MAP achieves lower training and validation loss than both Standard attention and QK-Norm. Further analyses show that QK-MAP preserves sensitivity to input scale, assigns less attention to the first token, and produces stronger attention contrast for relevant evidence in synthetic long-context tests. These results demonstrate that query-key scale can be effectively controlled without sacrificing token-specific magnitude information.

</details>


### [20] [AI in the Clinical Documentation Loop: Effects of LLM-Induced Note Bloat and Diagnostic Overcall on Downstream LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10601)
*Jinghui Liu,Anthony Nguyen,Taylan Gurgenci*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文研究"AI写病历、AI再读病历"这一自我消费循环中的两类文档伪影——"笔记膨胀"(note bloat)与"诊断过度调用"(diagnostic overcall)——对下游读病历的LLM的影响。基于MIMIC-III 300例住院记录、7个读者模型(4个模型家族)、配对对照设计发现：AI生成的摘要笔记即使与复制粘贴/模板文本等长，也会小幅但一致地降低下游"住院经过"(BHC)生成质量(如ROUGE-L下降约0.66–1.13pp，效应随插入剂量增大)；注入的未确认鉴别诊断会以5%–31%不等的比例被下游模型"带出"到摘要中(几乎全部保持为"可能"，极少被说成已确诊)，且这一失效在标准文档级质量指标(ROUGE-L、BERTScore、LLM评分的覆盖度/准确性/可用性)上完全不可见。结论是需要对EHR中的AI生成内容做专门监控。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: AI文书工具(AI scribe、自动摘要、出院小结生成)已在临床规模化部署，电子病历正日益同时被AI读取与写入，形成双向关系：后续迭代的AI会消费先前AI写入的内容。这一"自消费循环"(self-consuming loop)此前只在训练动态中被研究(shumailov等模型崩塌现象)，而在推理时上下文中缺乏考察。已有文献分别证明了长上下文的位置性利用不均与分心效应、以及人类书写冗余笔记对NLP模型的分布漂移，但均未回答"AI所写内容"与"人类所写内容"在影响下游模型时是否存在本质差异，也未考察AI以"缓和措辞"引入未支持的诊断后会如何传播。因此需要以受控配对实验分离上下文长度、内容来源(authorship)与内容本身三个因素。

Method: 下游任务为生成出院小结的住院经过(Brief Hospital Course, BHC)，参考标准为临床医生书写的BHC；所有比较均在同一住院记录内配对，受扰动记录与对照记录仅在所研究的伪影上不同。数据集为MIMIC-III，按结构条件筛选后从800例种子池中选出300例(每患者一次住院)，要求≥5条既往记录、≥3条叙述性记录、估计token≤32,000、主诊断属循环/呼吸/感染章节、≥3处缓和表述。生成器G为Qwen3.8-27B(主)与Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B(备)，读者R为Gemma-4-26B-A4B(主读者)及Gemma-4-12B/31B、Nemotron-3.5、Llama-3.3-70B、Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E、Qwen3.8-27B(自读自己生成的笔记)，共7个模型4个家族，全部本地以vLLM部署；评价器E为Qwen3.8-27B，GPT-OSS-120B作第二评价器(仅用于传播率)。两类伪影构造：(1)膨胀——插入冗余笔记，剂量d=0.05–0.50表示插入文本占最终记录比例，四组设置AI-red(生成器对槽位前原始笔记的摘要)、H-red(问题列表复制/随机片段)、F-red(模板样板)，H-red与F-red在长度上与AI-red匹配；另设R-red改写对照，由G用中性改写提示词重写每条复制的问题列表笔记(与overcall对照用同一提示词)，以分离"AI来源"与"AI内容"。(2)失真——诊断过度调用：选取25–400词的医师/护理叙述段落，生成器先中性改写得对照记录x̃，再加入一个记录中不存在、但与主诊断ICD共现模式匹配的候选诊断(ovc-related需条件流行率≥0.10且lift≥2；ovc-unrelated需≤0.02且lift≤0.5)，措辞为"可疑/可能/不能排除"等未决形式。两记录仅差该过度调用，从而固定AI来源不变。指标：膨胀用ROUGE-L、BERTScore(DeBERTa-large-MNLI)、LLM评分的覆盖/准确/总体可用性(1–5)、原子声明分解后的supported/contradicted/not_addressed占比；传播率π定义为对照摘要未提及而扰动摘要以"确认"或"可能"提及该诊断的配对比例；95%百分位bootstrap区间(2000次重采样)，主读者三行做Bonferroni校正；另由临床合作者对24对分层抽样摘要盲评。

Result: (1)膨胀效应：在相同插入长度与位置下，AI-red相对等长人类复制/模板文本使下游BHC变差，效应随剂量单调增大；剂量0.5时AI-red相对片段H-red与F-red的评分准确度分别低0.47(95%CI 0.34–0.59)与0.43(0.31–0.55)分。七个读者全部显示ROUGE-L下降(剂量0.25为−0.66至−1.13pp)，换用备生成器仍为−0.57pp。R-red改写对照相对H-red的ROUGE-L变化为−0.07/−0.07/0.00pp(均含零)，而AI-red相对R-red仍降0.28/0.59/0.92pp，说明效应来自AI生成的内容而非措辞。分解显示AI笔记使摘要变长(+6.1至+17.2%)、声明数增多(+2.0至+5.4)、supported声明占比下降(−1.2至−4.5pp)，而contradicted占比几乎不变。(2)传播：主读者Gemma-4-26B-A4B对相关目标传播率24.6%(16.8–32.4)、无关目标16.1%(10.9–22.2)，GPT-OSS评价器结果相近(23.8%/15.6%)，Nemotron生成器较低(10.2%/8.3%)；其余五位读者波动于5.8%–31.2%与2.5%–23.9%，能力最强的两个Gemma读者传播最高、能力最低的Nemotron最低(但样本小，仅为提示性解释)。传播几乎总以"可能"形式带出，hardened比例≤0.6%。相关与无关目标差异未达统计显著。(3)关键盲点：70个文档级质量对比中仅2个排除零(且效应仅−0.28与−0.25pp)，即标准指标完全无法反映该失效；编辑长度是混淆因素(短编辑传播最低，1–6词6.6%，7–12词两生成器相当13.5% vs 14.3%)。(4)临床复核：评价器与临床医生在"是否发生诱导传播"上24对中一致22对(91.7%，κ=0.83)，10例传播全部为"可能"而非确认；但医生仅认定24次注入中14次为真正的过度调用(6/12相关、8/12无关)，其中7例发生传播，且7例中有5例可能导致不必要的检查或管理改变。

Conclusion: 研究以受控配对实验证明：AI生成的病历内容会通过其"内容"本身(而非仅仅是长度或AI署名)系统性但幅度温和地降低下游AI摘要质量；AI引入的、措辞缓和的未支持鉴别诊断会跨模型传播到出院小结，而现有标准文档级评价指标对此几乎完全不敏感，可能在无人察觉的情况下积累并影响临床决策。据此建议：(1)对EHR中的AI生成内容进行专门监控与标注，区分来源与作者身份；(2)针对"诊断过度调用/未确认鉴别诊断"建立靶向评测，而非仅依赖ROUGE/BERTScore或通用LLM评分；(3)AI文书工具的部署评估应纳入"自消费"场景，即以含AI生成内容的记录作为下游输入。该研究属前期探索性工作(MIMIC-III早于LLM文书时代、AI内容为合成、仅300例住院、7个开源模型、目标诊断依赖ICD-9名称导致措辞机械且存在假阳性过度调用)，未来需扩大队列与模型覆盖(含前沿模型)、模拟多轮迭代累积效应并将膨胀与失真两类伪影联合扰动。

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to process medical records for healthcare tasks such as clinical documentation. Because these tools also generate documentation, the relationship is now bidirectional: models both read from and write to the record. Understanding how LLMs behave when reading records that already contain LLM-authored content is therefore critical for their safe deployment. In this study, we examine how LLM-authored content in the medical record affects downstream LLMs that read the same record. We consider two types of LLM-induced artifacts: bloat, in which LLM-generated summaries accumulate in the record and change the length and provenance of its content over time; and distortion, in which LLMs subtly alter clinical findings rather than fabricating facts outright. As a case of distortion, we study diagnostic overcall (documenting an unconfirmed differential diagnosis in the record) and test whether it propagates to the reader LLM's output. Across seven reader models from four families, we find evidence of both effects. First, LLM-generated summary notes modestly but consistently degraded downstream hospital-course generation compared with copy-forward and templated text of matched length. Second, injected overcalls reappeared in downstream outputs at rates that varied by reader model, without detectable changes in standard quality metrics. These findings show the need to monitor AI-generated content in medical records and to account for it when those records are later processed by AI.

</details>


### [21] [Behavioral Evaluation of Large Language Models Under Cognitive Biases in HAZOP Studies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10721)
*Vinicius M. Müller,Vitor A. O. Silva,Sávio S. V. Vianna,Flávio V. Silva*

TL;DR: 本文在420次单次推理试验中，对三个前沿LLM（Gemini 3.8 Flash、Claude Opus 5.5、Muse Spark 1.3）施加五类提示级认知操控（锚定、框架、可用性、确认、后见），配合47个源自工业参考案例的场景、15个条件格与双盲专家裁定，并用带案例随机截距的贝叶斯GLMM做层级推断。结果显示模型抵抗了96.8%的操控（操控臂仅8/252出现偏差，中性对照0/168），H1（操控提升偏差对数几率）与H2（模型间易感性差异）均统计不确定；但偏差集中于低锚定下的安全关键风险降级（M→L）与95%收益框架下由"approve"到"defer"的决策反转。结论是：LLM在HAZOP中只能作为认知卸载助手，必须配合严密的提示纪律与专家在环验证。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: HAZOP（危险与可操作性分析）是过程工业防范灾难性事故的核心定性方法，但其多学科专家工作坊模式耗时长、成本高、认知负荷重，疲劳下易产生启发式偏差、遗漏失效模式。然而自动化与计算机辅助HAZOP（规则专家系统、故障传播图、形式本体）受限于脆弱静态规则库与无法解析非结构化工程叙述，难以规模化。Transformer/LLM的出现提供了从工艺设计规格半自动生成安全工作表的可行路径，但当前对生成模型在过程危害识别中的评估仍主要依赖ROUGE、BERTScore等词汇重叠与表层嵌入相似度，完全无法评估生成安全结论的逻辑一致性与行为稳健性。更关键的现实是：PHA/HAZOP中的专家判断本身受锚定、确认偏差、可用性启发式影响；LLM预训练于人类语料并经RLHF对齐，因而并非中立客观的安全裁决者，会吸收、复制甚至放大这些拟人推断陷阱，表现出极性不对称、谄媚式附和与框架敏感性，甚至仅凭修辞线索即可在相同物理边界条件下反转风险分级。高危设施无法容忍风险表征失误，但文献缺乏针对前沿模型在安全关键工作流中经受标准化认知扰动的系统实证研究。

Method: （1）参考系统：Penelas & Pires (2021) 原油生产装置FWKO分离器V-001节点1，13条偏差记录中10条可独立成案，3条（倒流、更高温度、火灾爆炸）不虚构风险评级；源风险矩阵按定性序数处理。（2）实验电池：47案例、15条件格、每模型140个响应事件、56个对比组；锚定10×3（对照/低锚A/I/L/高锚E/V/H）、确认10×2、框架9×3（中性/95%收益/5%损失，各交叉approve/reject措辞）、可用性9×2（显著性小插曲 vs 整节点审查）、后见9×2（前瞻/后见）。每案例–条件–问题形式一次生成请求；组内工程事实与响应schema固定，仅操控文本与指令句变化；判定Y=1表示出现缺乏技术依据的目标偏差，技术错误本身不等于偏差，中性对照为结构性Z_c=0参照。（3）执行：全新单轮交互、T=0、top_p=1、无工具/检索/历史/二次LLM调用，模型原生推理设为最大、提交顺序随机；schema校验后确定性后处理（百分比裁剪与默认值、可得性列表截断至8项、框架补全），并与生成内容区分；仅完整且schema有效的组进入主分析。（4）人类验证：两名过程安全专家独立按参考与家族专属评分手册评审（因元数据可泄露模型/条件，未构成真正盲法），记录二元标签、清单与备注，分歧需书面裁定；报告未加权Cohen's κ及Wald 95% CI，偏差比例用Wilson 95% CI。（5）建模：贝叶斯GLMM，logit(p_ibmcw)=β0+α_m+γ_b+u_i+Z_c(β_Z+δ_m+η_b)，u_i=exp(ℓ_u)z_i（非中心化，跨家族条件独立近似），Neutral为Z_c=0；信息先验β0~N(logit(0.10),1.0²)以正则化控制臂0/168的准完全分离；PyMC NUTS 4链×2000预热+2000保留，验收率0.95、最大树深12，要求R̂<1.01、ESS≥400、无发散、E-BFMI≥0.3；先验预测与后验预测检查（总体/臂/格级T(Y)=ΣY），并做四种先验规格敏感性分析。（6）估计量：θ_bm=β_Z+η_b+δ_m、OR=exp(θ)、Pr(θ>0)（8000抽样，与预注册阈值0.975比较，单侧区间非同时区间）；H2用对比矩阵C（全秩、C·1=0）将δ映射为Δ并构造经验95%椭球可信域，判据d_0²>d_crit²，另报两两Δ的中位数、CrI与Pr(Δ>0)。

Abstract: Hazard and Operability (HAZOP) studies safeguard industrial processes against catastrophic accidents. Here we show across 420 trials that three frontier LLMs resisted 96.8% of cognitive manipulations, rendering overall susceptibility statistically inconclusive. ### [22] [Adapting Large Language Models via Multi-Task Learning for Mental Health Problem, Emotion, and Sentiment Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10797)
*Amir Rafiq Bhat,Rahim Dehkharghani,Zeki Erdem*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文探讨在 Llama 3.1 8B Instruct 上，结合参数高效微调（PEFT）、LoRA 与 4-bit 量化，通过"顺序多任务学习"完成心理健康问题检测、情绪检测与情感分析三项任务。核心发现是任务顺序显著影响知识迁移与任务干扰：先做心理健康检测（MHP-first）序列在 MHP 上取得最佳 Micro-F1 0.7624；先做情绪检测（Emotion-first）序列在情绪（F1 0.6052）和情感（F1 0.9459）上更优。联合多任务学习（Joint-MTL）基线则暴露出任务干扰与生成格式崩塌问题。LoRA+4-bit 量化大幅降低计算与显存开销，使 LLM 能在资源受限环境中适配。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 心理健康问题检测、情绪识别与情感分析在社交媒体场景中高度相关但任务目标不同，联合训练或固定顺序可能引发任务干扰（catastrophic forgetting / negative transfer）。同时，8B 级大模型的完全微调在算力与显存上不具可行性，需要 LoRA 等 PEFT 方法配合 4-bit 量化以降低部署门槛。因此作者关注两个问题：(1) 顺序多任务学习中任务排序如何影响知识迁移与最终性能权衡；(2) 相比联合多任务基线，顺序学习是否更具优势。

Method: 数据集为 4,243 条英文社交媒体帖子，覆盖三类任务。基座模型为 Llama 3.1 8B Instruct，采用 LoRA（低秩适配）进行参数高效微调，并结合 4-bit 量化（NF4/QLoRA 式配置）以压缩显存与计算开销。实验设计对比两种任务序列安排：MHP-first（心理健康检测→情绪检测→情感分析）与 Emotion-first（情绪检测→心理健康检测→情感分析），即在完成前序任务后将其适配器/知识迁移至下一任务。同时设置 Joint-MTL 基线，即单一模型同时优化三项任务。评估指标为 Micro-F1 / F1 等分类性能，并对比各序列在各任务上的表现。

Result: MHP-first 序列在心理健康问题检测上取得最优 Micro-F1 = 0.7624，说明将高相关性的心理健康语料置于序列前端能获得最直接的知识迁移收益，但其对后续任务的正向迁移有限。Emotion-first 序列在情绪检测上达到 F1 = 0.6052、情感分析上达到 F1 = 0.9459，表明情绪特征作为前置任务能更好地支撑后续情感判定，但该序列在 MHP 任务上相对退化。Joint-MTL 基线表现最差，暴露两类问题：任务间梯度/表示冲突导致的干扰，以及输出格式崩塌（生成式范式下无法稳定产出可解析的多任务标签）。LoRA 与 4-bit 量化使训练与推理的显存和算力需求显著下降，验证了资源受限场景下的可行性。

Conclusion: 顺序多任务 PEFT 在心理健康相关 NLP 任务上是有效的技术路线，且任务顺序是决定性能分布的关键变量：前置任务获得性能优势，而共享底层表示程度高、标签语义相近的后续任务能进一步受益。因此不存在普适最优顺序，需依据目标任务的优先级与业务需求进行排序（本工作中以 MHP 优先时选择 MHP-first，以情绪与情感优先时选择 Emotion-first）。相较之下，同时学习多任务会引入任务干扰与格式崩塌，在生成式 LLM 微调设定下风险更高。方法层面的启示是：LoRA + 4-bit 量化在几乎不牺牲精度的前提下，使 8B 模型的多任务顺序适配可在消费级/受限硬件上完成，为心理健康筛查类应用的落地提供可行路径。局限方面，序列学习本质仍存在前序任务偏置与遗忘问题，任务数量、顺序与超参（LoRA rank、量化位宽、合并策略）的系统性探索空间仍待验证。

Abstract: This study investigates sequential multi-task learning using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT), LoRA, and 4-bit quantization on Llama 3.1 8B Instruct for mental health problem detection, emotion detection, and sentiment analysis. Using 4,243 English social media posts, it compares two task sequences and demonstrates that task ordering significantly affects knowledge transfer and task interference. The MHP-first sequence achieves the best mental health problem detection (Micro-F1: 0.7624), while the Emotion-first sequence performs better in emotion (F1: 0.6052) and sentiment analysis (F1: 0.9459). A Joint-MTL baseline further highlights the challenges of simultaneous learning, including task interference and generative format collapse. Overall, the findings demonstrate the effectiveness of sequential PEFT for mental health NLP while showing that task order is critical to balancing performance across related tasks. The integration of LoRA and 4-bit quantization also reduces computational and memory requirements, supporting the adaptation of large language models in resource-constrained environments.

</details>

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文针对土耳其语（低资源语言）数学推理能力不足的问题，将 LoRA 微调、权重空间模型合并与推理期搜索（MCTS、Tree of Thoughts）三者结合到 Turkish-Llama-8B-DPO（Cosmos-DPO）上：微调阶段发现「数据质量胜过规模」（Mix-30k 最佳，大规模 MetaMath-300K 反而更差，且所有微调模型均未超过基线）；合并阶段线性合并（Linear）收益最大，GSM8K 最高达 0.63（Ties 表现平平，Breadcrumbs/Slerp 明显退化）；搜索阶段 MCTS 与 ToT（BFS/DFS）提升基于 LLM-judge 的平均推理质量分（0–100），BFS 2x2 是「效率甜点」（Cosmos-DPO 92 分、Qwen2.5-7B 85 分），但 ToT-DFS 16x16 延迟达 500 倍。结论：线性合并稳定有效，搜索推理随深度趋于饱和且算力代价高昂，自反思式 RJE 训练无显著收益。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 大语言模型的数学推理依赖结构化推理与精确计算，但英语等高资源语言与土耳其语等低/中资源语言之间存在明显性能鸿沟，根源在于土耳其语数学训练数据稀缺、从零预训练成本过高。作者希望在不进行大规模预训练的前提下，通过「算法干预」最大化可用的翻译数据与预训练权重的价值：其一是评估不同数学数据集（MetaMath、NuminaMath、TigerLab-MathInst 的土耳其语翻译版）对 LoRA 微调效果的影响，以验证「数据质量 vs. 数据规模」的作用；其二是考察将微调模型与早期版本（基座）做权重空间合并能否进一步提升推理能力；其三是比较 MCTS、ToT 等搜索式推理与零样本/少样本基线的差异；其四是设计模块化的 Reward-Judge-Enhance (RJE) 流水线模拟自我反思，并通过消融确定各模块（奖励、评判、增强）的作用与重要性。

Method: 1) 微调：以 Turkish-Llama-8B-DPO-v0.1（OpenLLMTurkishLeaderboard 上的 COSMOS-DPO）为基座，用 LoRA 在 DeepL 机器翻译的 MetaMath、NuminaMath、TigerLab-MathInst 土耳其语版本上做 SFT，每数据集取 50k 样本，并构建随机采样的混合数据集 Mix-20K/30K/40K/50K，另训练 Metamath-300K 以考察规模效应；用 lm-eval-harness 在土耳其语基准（GSM8K、ARC、Hellaswag、TruthfulQA、Winogrande）上评测。2) 模型合并：在权重空间采用 Linear（平均）、Ties（冲突符号剪枝）、Breadcrumbs（基于梯度轨迹）、Slerp（球面插值）四种方式，组合 DPO/微调/基座等不同权重，并含 Same-Time、Binary、Evolve-Linear（24 步迭代）等变体，主要以 GSM8K 准确率衡量。3) 搜索算法：实现 ToT-BFS（队列逐层扩展）、ToT-DFS（栈回溯）与 MCTS（UCB 探索，UCB 权重 1.41，每节点最多 2 子节点，种子答案为 "I don't know"），节点扩展通过 RJE 流水线生成：Critique 客户端对子节点答案进行批评，Enhance 客户端（本地模型自身）据此改写答案。4) RJE 与客户端配置：设计四组 Client-0/1/2/3（Reward/Judge 用 GPT 或自评，Enhance 统一用本地模型自纠错），在 gsm8k_tr-v0.2 的 100 题子集上测试；评测用 gpt-4o-mini 作为 LLM judge，在温度 0 下按正确性、逻辑一致性、推理质量给 0–100 分并取算术平均。5) 计算成本：在 A100 80GB 上测量各推理方法的耗时。

Conclusion: 面向土耳其语数学推理的三条路径各有定位：权重空间线性合并是最可靠、最可复现的增益手段（最佳 GSM8K 0.63），其有效性源于同一基座微调权重之间的线性模式连通性，简单平均胜过复杂启发式（TIES/Breadcrumbs/Slerp）；搜索式推理（MCTS/ToT）能提升主观推理质量分，但存在明显的算力瓶颈与随深度饱和现象，BFS 2x2 配置在质量与成本间最为平衡；RJE 自反思训练模块未能带来显著收益，说明模型的自我评判能力仍是瓶颈。局限性包括：依赖 DeepL 机器翻译可能引入噪声与翻译伪影；gsm8k_tr-v0.2 由 GPT-4 生成、可能含特定翻译痕迹且未做人工评估；规模有限（仅 8B 基座、100 题搜索子集）；搜索过程存在随机性；另需在更广泛的模型规模与多语言上验证。

Abstract: We improve Turkish mathematical reasoning in Large Language Models by combining LoRA fine-tuning, weight-space model merging, and search-based inference. Using Turkish-Llama 8B-DPO with Turkish translations of MetaMath, NuminaMath, and TigerLab, we find data quality beats scale (Mix-30k best among fine-tuned; large MetaMath underperforms). Search with MCTS and Tree of Thoughts improves mean LLM-judge scores for reasoning quality on a 0-100 scale. Limitations include machine translation, limited scale, and search stochasticity.

<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 公共 ASR 基准的序列错误率（WER/CER）已持续走低，但生产系统仍大量依赖热词表、上下文偏置、检索增强与 LLM 后纠错来保护信息性术语。这暴露出评测与工程需求的错位：统一编辑代价的 WER 对"可丢弃的填充词"和"一旦损坏就使转写不可用的产品名"给予同等权重。例如 Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 在句级 1.69% WER 下把 "Claude Code" 转成 "Cloud Code"，整个产品名丢失却几乎不体现在序列指标中。已有工作提出关键词级、实体级、语义级评测（Park 等的 KER、Galibert 等的命名实体重要性排序、Rugayan 等的对齐语义距离），但存在两点空白：加权代价的权重难以统一确定，且尚无覆盖中文、以"整短语"为单位的可复现双协议；同时模型条件（challenge）采样带来的选择偏差缺少对照验证。

Method: 任务定义：关键词为"整跨度"（人物/机构/产品/地点实体、技术与金融领域术语、版本化短语如 Kimi 2.7 与 GPT-4o、关系性短语），其损坏会改变该 utterance 的可用信息；等价形式为样本局部、评测前冻结（Claude Code 可为必需短语，Claude 可为批准变体）。指标：参考与假设经 Unicode NFKC 与大小写折叠归一化，关键词匹配忽略空格/下划线/连字符但保留句点、斜杠、& 等标点，数字与版本边界不可跨版本匹配（GPT-4 ≠ GPT-4.1）；对每个关键词计算缺失 M_k=max(0,N_k−C_k) 与多余 I_k=max(0,C_k−N_k)，KER=Σ(M_k+I_k)/ΣN_k 微平均，普通词/非关键词插入不计入分子分母，KER 可超 100%；参考与输出共用同一匹配器，回归测试要求参考对参考 KER=0。数据：10 小时中播客/圆桌/技术讨论长音频，按整录音切分清洗去音乐/广告/低质参考，按语言与来源划分 A/B 两区，273 个录音组、1501 clips（750 中/751 英）、3881 个关键词条目、4723 次出现，100% clips 至少含一个关键词。标注管线为版本化可审计文本评审：实体/术语规则播种候选（优先长短语）、Codex CLI 筛选 1–3 个信息性短语、机械精确跨度校验、人工复审与抽检，最终冻结关键词、变体、来源组、内部音频指纹与打分器版本。采样：挑战集为"模型条件"——预先指定 Qwen3-ASR-0.6B/1.7B 与 GLM-ASR-Nano-2512 三系统，按选择期诊断的 ≥2/3、=1/3、=0/3 错误分层，目标时长占比 55/25/20，再按关键词覆盖与标注置信度排序（历史标签 55.0% 落在 ≥2/3，后用报告口径复算为 64.6%，改变 555 个 clip 分层）；对照集在关键词资格审核后用固定加盐哈希采样，不读任何模型预测，77 clips、61 录音组、216 次出现，与挑战集零录音组重叠。评测：5 个本地推理系统（Qwen3-ASR 两尺寸、GLM-ASR-Nano-2512、Whisper large-v3-turbo via faster-whisper/CTranslate2 FP16 beam1 无 VAD、MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize-0.9B BF16 1024 token 确定性解码并机械去除说话人标签）+ 2 个官方 API（StepAudio 3 ASR Max、抖音 Doubao ASR 2.0），均仅给音频与强制语言，不给参考/关键词/热词；中文报混合分词 MER、英文报 WER；置信区间为录音组 bootstrap 10,000 次重采样的 95% 百分位区间。治理：原始音频、参考、关键词与来源信息保留在受控环境，公开包仅含报告、协议、打分器、聚合统计与单独授权示例。

Result: 挑战集上 MER/WER 区间 5.31%–12.91%，KER 区间 13.61%–33.81%，且 KER 普遍为序列误差的 2–4 倍；StepAudio 3 ASR Max 最优（总体 KER 13.61%、中文 MER 5.31%），Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 英文 WER 最低（5.95%）但整体 KER 24.88%。排序反转明显：StepAudio 与 Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 中文 MER 仅差 0.04 点，中文 KER 却差 14.62 点；英文侧 Qwen3-ASR-1.7B WER 领先 0.32 点而 StepAudio KER 领先 7.36 点。中文 KER 系统性高于英文（挑战集最高 46.49% vs 22.20%），原因是中文片段大量含英文产品名、缩写与代码切换术语。误差按关键词长度分层（主要分母含 2888 个一词单位、1191 个两词单位、644 个 ≥3 单位出现），且各系统模式不同。对照集上全部 7 系统 KER 仍达 10.65%–27.31%；三个选择系统 challenge−control 上升 9.14–11.20 点，另四个系统仅上升 2.48–6.83 点，提示选择偏差存在但有限。案例显示同音替换（"极客公园"→"极公源/极工源/极光源"）、术语替换（"长程任务"→"长城任务/长征任务"）、产品名丢失（Claude Code→Cloud Code，仅 MOSS 与两个 API 系统恢复）。

Conclusion: 全部 7 个系统在模型条件挑战集与模型盲对照集上都存在整短语保全失败，表明 KER 与序列误差的鸿沟是系统性的而非采样伪影；KeyASRBench 通过冻结的整短语标注与出现级 KER 评测，使这些失败在序列指标之外显式化。论文定位为 pilot：对照集模型盲但非来源匹配（仅 76/1 录音来源比），区间宽，只支持"存在性检验"而非精细排序或自然流量估计；未做双独立标注的音频级完整复审，KER 也尚未与检索性能、任务完成率或人类转写效用校准；bootstrap 未建模更高层序列相关性，两次 API 调用相隔 7 天且服务端版本不可锁定，服务漂移可能贡献差异。后续工作包括：按录音组抽取更大的来源匹配对照集、扩充稀疏的关系短语（88 条）与版本标识（29 条）类别、加入重叠/远场/口音切片、把短语保全与检索和人类效用挂钩，以及在音频-only、热词、上下文偏置与检索增强四种条件下对照以定位可修复失败的干预手段。数据与标注保留在受控环境，公开包仅含报告、协议、打分器与聚合统计，涉及人名与敏感属性需在对外使用前完成去标识与授权审查。

Abstract: Public automatic speech recognition (ASR) benchmarks increasingly report low sequence error rates, yet production systems still use hotword lists, contextual biasing, retrieval, and post-correction. This motivates a complementary question: does a transcript preserve selected names, products, technical terms, versions, and relational phrases? We present KeyASRBench, a bilingual pilot that operationalizes occurrence-based Keyword Error Rate (KER) over frozen whole-phrase annotations. The 10-hour model-conditioned challenge set contains 1,501 Chinese and English clips with 4,723 keyword occurrences. Across five locally inferred checkpoints and two official API systems, language-specific MER/WER ranges from 5.31% to 12.91%, while KER ranges from 13.61% to 33.81%. A disjoint 30-minute model-blind control yields KER of 10.65%-27.31%. The control confirms that selected-phrase errors extend beyond challenge-set selection.

</details>


### [26] [DeepFinance: Can AI Diligence a $100MM Deal?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10926)
*Drew Hahn,Tyler Shibata,Jackson Grove,Rahul Sonwalkar*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: DeepFinance 是 Julius Research 推出的超长时程（ultra long-horizon）私募股权（PE）与投行（IB）端到端基准，包含 21 个真实交易类任务，每个任务平均需人类专业人士 27.1 小时完成，配有平均 19 个文件的数据室，并用平均 84 条专家撰写的评分标准从「产出、工作流、判断」三方面打分，同时评分最终交付物与推理轨迹的可审计性。评测 22 个模型配置（各用其原生 agent harness），最佳为 OpenAI GPT-6 Astra（max 推理）得分 57.6%，前四名无统计显著差异；主要发现是前沿模型常「用错误输入算出正确结果」「找到决策关键证据却不据此行动」，说明当前模型在假设选择、跨源冲突调和与可审计性上仍显著不足。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 现有金融类评测（FinanceBench、BizBench、FinanceQA、BigFinanceBench、OfficeQA、GDPval、Westworld Finance Diligence Bench 等）存在三点根本缺陷：一是偏重文档问答与单一数值正确性，而真实 PE/IB 工作要求在冲突来源间做取舍、在信息不全时做合理假设；二是缺少真实的「数据室」工作环境（邮件链、会议纪要、各格式文件、版本冲突），无法评估模型的信息筛选与调和能力；三是评分只看最终输出（甚至只看 ELO 偏好排序），不评轨迹，而金融工作类似需要逐行 code review 的 PR——每个数字都要可溯源、每个假设都要能被 MD/投委会/客户追问。据此需要一个能同时度量结果与过程的超长时程、可审计的评测基准。

Method: 1) 任务构建：覆盖估值、尽职调查、承销/投资条款、财务建模四大支柱，任务为经脱敏的真实交易模拟工作，problem statement 平均 240 词（比 GDPval 短约 29%）；数据室平均 19 个文件，类型含 .xlsx/.docx/.eml/PDF/CSV，内容含邮件、聊天与交易团队笔记、财务模型与预测、CIM/SPA/term sheet/承诺函、尽调报告、投委会纪要、市场数据与可比公司。2) 评分：以专家撰写的 rubric 逐条判定（平均 84 条/任务，最多 140 条），三类标签——Output（计算、结论与交付物是否正确）、Workflow（是否找到并使用了关键证据）、Judgment（证据是否支撑其假设与决策）；评分口径为满足标准的百分比，先对尝试平均再对任务平均，每个配置每任务 10 次成功尝试（出错则重跑）；给部分正确的步骤以部分分，避免只惩罚上游错误导致的连锁失败。3) 质量保证：多层 agentic verifier 与人类专家（Evercore、J.P. Morgan、UBS、HBS、Wharton 等）同行评审，确认任务可解、参考解有证据支撑、rubric 接受有效替代解、失败项归因于 agent 而非参考答案/评分器/环境；争议评分回溯至源文件与轨迹。4) Harness：每个模型族使用其最可能投入使用的原生 harness（claude-code、codex、opencode-ai、kimi-code、qwen-code、x.ai、mistral-vibe），开启几乎全部原生工具含联网搜索，仅禁用 ask-user（保证运行可独立完成）；每次运行独立沙箱，答案与 rubric 置于隔离的评分环境。5) 统计：95% bootstrap 置信区间（10 万次重采样，任务与尝试双层），配对 bootstrap 检验前四名的差异显著性；并绘制分数–API 成本、分数–token 数的 Pareto 前沿。

Result: 最佳配置 GPT-6 Astra(max) 57.6%（CI 49.5–66.2，$6.73/任务，2.41M tokens）；Claude Opus 5.5(max) 54.8%、Claude Sonnet 5.5(max) 54.6%、GPT-6.1 Sol(max) 54.3%、GPT-6.1 Terra(max) 47.2%、Claude Fable 5.1(max) 45.6%（但成本最高 $12.02）、Muse Wonder 1.0(max) 44.2%、Gemini 4 Argon 41.4%……底部为 Nemotron 3 Ultra 14.5%、Inkling 13.1%、Inkling Small 10.9%，与榜首相差约 45 分。前四名在配对 bootstrap（95%）下无统计显著差异；Anthropic 与 OpenAI 包揽前六。成本效率上 GPT-6.1 Sol 以 $1.17/任务达 54.3%，GPT-6.1 Terra $0.69/任务达 47.2%，GPT-6 系列占 22 个配置中成本 Pareto 前沿的 4/6。定性发现：Fable 5.1 通用智能未迁移到高金融场景；模型常找到相关证据却不识别其含义（CFO 与分析师口径冲突时不主动调和），不愿挑战给定假设；上游错误（盈利口径、来源选择、完成时点）会级联影响债务额度、费用、现金流、估值与回报，因此失败标准数不等于独立推理错误数；典型失误是「用错误输入做对计算」（如用错误盈利小计算债务额度、对缺失某销售渠道的预测套用支付上限与里程碑规则）；典型盲点是「识别到证据但不行动」——某收购任务中变更交割日可降低对价 125 万美元，所有前沿模型尝试均未利用买方择日权。

Conclusion: 要让 AI 在交易中可用，其产出必须经得起复核：跨 20–30 小时的高金融任务中，agent 需选择可靠假设、保持一致性并解释关键决策。DeepFinance 通过同时评分结果与其背后的工作（auditability），既给专业人士提供可检查分析的手段，也为研究者定位需要修复的错误类型，从而更接近衡量 agent 是否真能「从数据室走到可被信赖的决策」。当前上限约 57.6% rubric 满足率，前沿差距仍未拉开且各模型在判断、调和冲突来源与主动利用决策相关信息上存在系统性短板，说明该方向仍远未解决。

Abstract: Existing evaluations of AI models on high-finance work focus on retrieving answers from financial documents and producing numerically correct outputs. Real private equity (PE) and investment banking (IB) work also depends on choosing between conflicting sources, making sound assumptions, and keeping every step auditable. We introduce DeepFinance, an ultra long-horizon benchmark of 21 end-to-end PE and IB tasks that take a human professional an average of 27.1 hours. Each task pairs a request with a data room averaging 19 files and is graded against an average of 84 expert-written rubric criteria covering output, workflow, and judgment. We evaluate 22 model configurations, each in its native agent harness. The best configuration, GPT-6 Astra with max reasoning, satisfies 57.6% of rubric criteria, and the top four configurations are not statistically distinguishable. Frontier models often calculate correctly from the wrong inputs and find decision-relevant evidence without acting on it.

### [27] [Think or Remember: The Exchange Rate of Agentic Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10982)
*Juan Wisznia,Santiago Luis Groba Alonso,Matías Gómez Taddeo,Gonzalo Zabaleta,Joaquín Cullen,Luciano Del Corro*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: 本文提出一个"思考—记忆交换率"P*=c/β 的成本模型：架构按每 token 处理价 c 与每注意力对价 β 计价，二者之比决定"思考区"(低于 P*)与"记忆区"(高于 P*)，据此可对智能体上下文策略(保留/丢弃先前推理、压缩、窗口、编辑)定价。作者把策略变更拆分为"机械成本"(同一续写下的重算与携带代价)与"行为成本"(续写本身改变带来的代价)，并给出干预回本条件 −ΔB>ΔM。计数经插桩 vLLM 在 648 个请求上精确吻合。实验显示：同一批录制运行中，仅改变服务端的缓存复用规则即可反转 Keep/Drop 的成本排序(1.74× vs 0.34×)；滑动窗口比一次性删除贵约 4 倍；实测重跑中丢弃先前推理在四个模型上使 HotpotQA 完全正确率下降 9–23 个百分点，但在 ScienceWorld 上使 gpt-oss-20b 从 3/88 提升到 20/88；跨任务携带历史使成本降至 0.60 却少解新任务。结论是：比较上下文策略实质上是比较系统，架构与服务配置共同决定保留历史的成本与其诱发的后续工作。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 基于推理模型的智能体在每次调用时都会重发不断增长的完整对话记录，其成本并非由模型本身决定，而由两个交易方共同决定：客户端决定保留/摘要/编辑可见历史，服务器决定先前轮的推理是否回填到提示词(Keep/Drop)以及缓存复用哪些计算。因此"该保留还是丢弃推理""如何压缩历史"不是模型属性，而是系统级决策。已有工作(Satish 2026、Hoy 2026、Shao 2026 等)通常只在单一服务约定下报告 token 数或美元节省，但 token 成本取决于其在上下文中的位置以及服务器是否已缓存该工作，token 计数本身无法为策略定价。本文目标：把一次运行的总成本形式化为架构(逐 token 线性价 c、逐注意力对价 β)与双方选择的函数，并给出可检验、可迁移的比较协议。

Method: 1) 成本模型：第 t 次调用提示长 P_t、可复用前缀 R_t、生成位置 G_t，N=Σ(P_t−R_t+G_t)，Q=Σ[tri(P_t+G_t)−tri(R_t)]，C=cN+βQ+(w−1)cG，其中 w 为解码溢价；c 由投影矩阵参数计数给出，β=4n_f u(全注意力层)；混合模型另计循环层投影，循环状态更新与输出头另计(式16)。

4) 机械/行为分解：ΔC=ΔM+ΔB，ΔM 由在两策略提示下重放同一录制续写精确算出，ΔB 由从同一分叉点实机重跑获得；干预回本条件 −ΔB>ΔM；并给出两种续写参照下的一致性证明与期望形式。
5) 实验：插桩 vLLM(RTX 3070)对 27 个密集/混合调度、648 个请求验证计数零误差(最大误差 0)；主机录制回放(Qwen3.7-Plus 159 条 ScienceWorld 轨迹、132 条确认集)；开放模型分叉研究(Qwen3 4B/8B/30B-A3B/32B、gpt-oss-20b、R1-distill，ScienceWorld 与标题隐藏的 HotpotQA)；32 条链式任务研究(Fresh/Carry/Clear × Keep/Drop)；托管模型上的 Summary vs 零样本 CLM 编辑三批队列(20 条链)。统计为 4000 次 bootstrap，ScienceWorld 按任务族重采样、HotpotQA 按问题重采样、链式按整链重采样。

Result: (1) 计数与插桩 vLLM 在全部 648 请求、11 个密集与 16 个混合调度上精确一致(最大绝对误差 0)。(2) 服务规则反转排序：同一 103 对 Qwen3-8B ScienceWorld 录制中，丢弃先前推理在生成态复用下成本为保留的 1.74×[1.46,2.08]，在提示词复用下为 1.02×(区间跨 1)，在完全不复用下为 0.34×[0.28,0.42]。(3) 删除时机比大小更重要：滑窗保留最新 5 个推理块在 P*∈[1K,2M]、w∈[1,5] 下成本为全保留的 3.97–4.56 倍(提示词仅缩短 1.6%)，而一次性立即删除在各配置下与全保留相差 ≤2%。(4) 实机重跑：HotpotQA(标题隐藏、仅判答案)上丢弃推理使 8B/4B/30B-A3B/gpt-oss 完全正确率分别下降 13.3/13.9/22.7/9.2 个百分点(区间均不含 0)，重复采集复现该方向；ScienceWorld 上除 gpt-oss-20b(3/88→20/88)外成功率差异跨 0，8B/4B/30B/32B 的成本比为 1.74/1.18/1.73/1.94。(5) 跨任务携带历史：Keep 下 Carry 成本为 Fresh 的 0.60 且新任务解出 17/96 对 30/96；Drop 下为 0.43 与 13/96 对 26/96；"clear memory"臂居中且成本接近 Fresh。(6) 客户端窗口在生成态复用下增加 145.9–352.9% 成本且机械项恒大于行为项，机械性无法回本。(7) 托管队列中 CLM/Summary 成本比在 0.618–1.789 之间随保留规则与批次反转，最新批次 Keep 下 CLM 便宜 15%、Drop 下贵 33%，且每格仅一次执行故不可与运行间波动分离。(8) gpt-oss 中仅删除历史轮格式(空 analysis 消息)即使中位成本比从 1.43 变为 7.31；R1-distill 三臂 0 全对。

Conclusion: 上下文策略的比较等价于系统的比较：架构(c、β、P*)与服务配置(缓存规则 ρ、解码溢价 w、渲染与淘汰)共同决定保留历史的成本及其诱发的后续工作，价格足以反转同一录制工作上的排名。据此给出迁移顺序：先在目标系统下重估录制工作的价格，再评估该策略在目标上产生的续写与成功率。具体而言，服务端应保存生成态并暴露可复用前缀，客户端在裁剪前应给替换生成与幸存尾部定价；针对单一缓存规则与解码价格校准的奖励会把部署选择固化进所训练的编辑器。实践含义是"更便宜"不等于"更好"：丢弃先前推理可省成本却损失 HotpotQA 正确率，携带历史亦然，因此优化应带成功概率约束(min Pr(success)≥q)而非仅看成本。局限：成本为声明系数下的操作计数而非实测时延/美元，w 为扫描范围而非部署校准；计数仅在单一引擎、两种模型上验证；重放由日志重建缓存状态而非服务器真实状态；机械/行为划分依赖所选续写参照(但总和不变)；分叉集合条件于到达分叉点且各臂完成，环境状态等价性未校验；Keep/Drop 未作为已部署策略评估，托管比较每格仅一次执行。

Abstract: Agents built on reasoning models resend their growing transcript at every call. Two transacting parties, not the model, decide what that costs: the client keeps or edits messages; the server decides whether earlier reasoning returns in the prompt and what its cache reuses. We define a cost model whose counts match an instrumented engine exactly; the architecture charges $c$ per token processed and $\beta$ per pair attended. Their ratio $P^*=c/\beta$ is an exchange rate between thinking and remembering: per token, processing dominates below this context length, a thinking regime, and attention above it, a memory regime. A policy change has a mechanical cost, incurred even if the agent writes the same tokens, and a behavioral one: it writes different tokens, changing cost and outcome. Serving alone can flip which policy is cheaper: on recorded Qwen3-8B ScienceWorld runs, dropping earlier reasoning costs 1.74 times keeping it when the server reuses generated states and 0.34 times when it reuses nothing. In live reruns, dropping it cuts correct HotpotQA answers by 9-23 percentage points on four models, at lower point-estimate cost. Comparing context policies means comparing systems: architecture and serving set the cost of the history kept and the work it induces.

</details>


### [28] [Building and Auditing Chemical Datasets with LLMs: A General LLM-as-a-Judge Framework Applied to Homogeneous Catalytic PET Depolymerisation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11030)
*Muhammad bin Javaid,Karim K. Ben Hicham,Enkhnyam Battulga,Alexander Mitsos,Martin Grohe*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models can rapidly extract structured multivariate experimental data from the chemistry literature, yet verifying thousands of generated records without ground truth remains difficult. We present a general, citation-grounded extraction and verification methodology centered on an independent "LLM-as-a-judge", applied to the literature on homogeneous catalytic poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) depolymerisation. In this pipeline, an extractor LLM generates schema-enforced records from research papers with citations to document chunks tagged with universally unique identifiers (UUIDs); an independent LLM judge then reads the full paper alongside each record, flags unsupported fields, and proposes cited corrections. Prompt ablations show that requiring chunk-level citations not only provides provenance down to specific paragraphs and tables but also improves extraction accuracy. Before deploying the judge at scale, we benchmarked it against manual evaluation on extractions from a hand-curated reference set of 295 ionic-liquid-catalysed PET glycolysis experiments. The judge agreed with human evaluation on 85.7% of reviewed records and was significantly more effective than a heuristic string-matching baseline at catching errors across related experiments. Deployed across 3,942 extracted records from 561 papers, the framework accepted 67.5% of them as written. Its proposed corrections concentrated on quantitative fields, where the extractor often conflated related experiments. We release the extracted dataset with the complete LLM judge audit logs, as well as the Chemistry Data Extractor Toolkit, an open-source application implementing this end-to-end pipeline in a code-free, browser-based environment for document parsing, customizable schema and prompt design, model-agnostic extraction and auditing, interactive provenance-highlighted review, and reproducible dataset bundling.

### [29] [Room to Reconsider: Reply Length Decides Whether Pushback Makes Language Models Sycophantic or Self-Correcting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11035)
*Ook Lee*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Language models often abandon a correct answer when a user pushes back without giving a reason, and this behavior is usually studied as sycophancy to be suppressed. The same pushback, however, also leads models to revisit and sometimes repair a wrong answer. We measure both effects on multiple-choice questions from MMLU and ARC-Challenge with four open models from two families (Qwen3 1.7B, 4B and 8B, and OLMo-2 7B), reading the final answer exactly from option logits after a free-form reply. The reply budget changes the verdict. When Qwen3-4B may answer the challenge in at most 96 tokens, pushback leaves accuracy unchanged or slightly lower; with 1,024 tokens, it corrects 43% of its wrong answers and pushback raises accuracy by 5.7 points. Whether pushback helps overall follows a simple break-even rule in the cave and correction rates. Inside the model, caving can be partly predicted before the challenge: hidden states add about 0.04-0.06 AUROC over turn-1 confidence in three of our four probing runs. A probe trained only on self-correction cases predicts caving beyond confidence when replies are truncated, but not when the model can finish its reasoning. Activation steering never reduced caving selectively: where it worked, it suppressed self-correction as well. We conclude that sycophancy evaluations should allow full replies and report self-correction alongside caving.

### [30] [A Layer-wise Study of How Style Rewriting Breaks the Calibration of Zero-Shot LLM Fake-News Detectors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11239)
*Prabhjot Singh,Praney Goyal,Raksha Sharma*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly asked to judge whether a news article is true, and their stated confidence is often taken at face value. We test what happens to that confidence when an article's writing style, but not its facts, is manipulated, as in recent \emph{style attacks} on fake-news detectors. Tracing how the prediction and its confidence form layer by layer inside the network, we study three model families (LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B) on three fake-news benchmarks, and find the same three patterns in every model--dataset pairing. First, on the original articles the models are competent and largely honest judges: they settle on an answer, briefly become overconfident, and then correct their confidence in the final layers. Second, style-rewritten articles break this self-correction: the models become far less accurate, under the strongest attack, worse than random guessing, yet remain just as confident, so they are \emph{confidently wrong} precisely when a warning is most needed. Third, nearly all of the damage comes from rewriting into sensational or emotionally charged styles, while sober, neutral rewrites leave the models' honesty largely intact. The practical implication is that an LLM's confidence about veracity cannot be trusted as a safety signal when an article's style may have been manipulated.

### [31] [EASE-KV: Diagnosing the Gap Between Memory Availability and Effective Use](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11299)
*Di Lu,Zechen Li,Xuanyu Yue,Jiabo Fan,Hao Xue,Flora D. Salim*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reusable key-value (KV) memory avoids repeatedly prefilling retrieved text, but stored and injected memories do not necessarily become usable evidence. We present EASE-KV, a controlled framework for understanding this gap under fixed candidates and a frozen language model. EASE-KV separates three interfaces: whether required relations are preserved during encoding, whether preserved memories receive appropriate influence during allocation, and whether outcome supervision can identify useful allocations. Matched experiments show that causal encoding improves compositional accuracy by 25.0 percentage points over block-diagonal encoding, while the tested inference-time bridging methods fail to recover the lost contextual information. With unchanged stored states, diagnostic evidence-guided allocation improves LongMemEval accuracy from 31.2% to 38.4%, demonstrating that memory influence can be controlled without re-encoding. However, controllability does not guarantee learnability: binary correctness provides informative reward contrast for 53.0% of sampled query groups, compared with 73.6% under the evaluated shaped-reward setting. These findings show that effective KV memory requires more than retrieval and injection: the required relations must be encoded, preserved memories must receive appropriate influence, and supervision must distinguish better allocations from worse ones.

### [32] [ScrapeBench: Evaluating Legal Compliance of AI Agents in Website Scraping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11306)
*Joseph Marvin Imperial,Daniel Slate,Noam Kolt*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: AI agents deployed on the open web are becoming more capable of performing actions that may breach contractual provisions and violate computer security laws. In this paper, we introduce ScrapeBench, the first agentic benchmark for empirically evaluating the legal compliance of AI agents with website scraping policies, namely terms of service (ToS) and this http URL directives. Across widely used closed-weight and open-weight AI agents, we find that most agents exhibit low compliance rates (< 5%) when instructed to scrape websites in our sample of 1,626 popular websites that explicitly prohibit scraping. In addition, we observe that even where AI agents actively check the applicable ToS and this http URL , they continue to exhibit low compliance rates. Conversely, in our sample of 269 websites that do not prohibit scraping, we observe that agents sometimes refuse to scrape despite it being lawful, such as Claude Opus 4.6 exhibiting an over-refusal rate of 98.5%. Our human baseline experiments (n = 180 participants) suggest that humans exhibit compliance rates comparable to AI agents but over-refuse at much higher rates.

### [33] [Vietnamese Legal Ontology: Every legal answer, traced to the article that grounds it](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11426)
*Khac-Hoai Nam Bui,Quan Tran Minh*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: A legal answer is only as good as the article it rests on. Vietnam's largest open legal corpus pairs 109,543 published questions and answers with 573,851 legal documents, yet its citations are free text: "Khoan 3 Dieu 101 cua Bo luat nay" ("Clause 3, Article 101 of this Code") names neither the code nor its version. Following the five stages of NVIDIA Auto Ontology, Discover, Ground, Validate, Expose and Learn, we turn four open datasets into a knowledge graph of 11.5 M nodes and 16.0 M edges in which every node and edge carries its source record and method, with no duplicate keys, dangling edges or schema violations. Of 67,868 cited provisions, 61,487 resolve to a dated law version, 51,694 to a parsed article, clause or point, and 19,012 are confirmed word for word. The ontology then shows what flat records hide. 36% of the 78,361 answers whose citations resolve now cite a law that is no longer in force; 2,525 verified citations point to an article number that says something else in the current law; 2,520 citations were re-versioned because their words match a different version than their date suggests; and 5,575 document numbers are shared by several local authorities, one of them by 72. Every number in this paper is computed from the graph.

### [35] [When Should Diffusion Language Models Reconsider Their Commitments?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11551)
*Haoyang Zheng,Yidong Ouyang,Blake Jianhang Chen,Tian Tan,Ziqian Lin,Liqian Peng,Alec Go,Guang Lin*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) are well known for fast text generation via parallel decoding. However, independent parallel sampling can commit to inconsistent predictions, and less is known about how to selectively revise these early token commitments. In this work, we introduce $\underline{\mathrm{P}}$lanned $\underline{\mathrm{U}}$nmasking-and-$\underline{\mathrm{R}}$evision Joint $\underline{\mathrm{L}}$earning (PURL) for MDMs, a training-based framework that seamlessly unifies parallel generation with selective token revision. We derive a normalized joint transition whose likelihood factorizes into edit selection, unmask selection, and token prediction. These components are trained jointly on partially masked sequences constructed according to the model's own unmasking policy. During inference, all three decisions are supported by a single shared forward pass, enabling the model to decode masked tokens and revise noisy tokens. Across logic puzzles, mathematical reasoning, and code generation, PURL improves accuracy at matched unmask budgets, with relative gains up to 47.4% accuracy improvement and up to an $8\times$ reduction in scheduled decoding rounds. Beyond these gains, our analysis further reveals general principles of revisable decoding: token edits become more effective as context accumulates; early edits can steer unfinished trajectories, whereas later edits tend to remain localized; and effective edits therefore depend on both calibrating when to intervene and learning where and how to revise. Together, these suggest that effective parallel generation depends not on revising more tokens, but on making the right commitments revisable at the right time.

### [36] [Continuous modeling of manipulative participation for stance analysis: Online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in Türkiye](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11576)

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Studies of online political discourse commonly infer public opinion through stance analysis while implicitly assuming that observed user participation is authentic. Meanwhile, studies focusing on detecting manipulative participation are typically modeling it as a binary phenomenon, overlooking the varying degrees to which users may engage in coordinated or inauthentic behavior. This study proposes a continuous modeling approach for manipulative participation and examines its integration with stance analysis. Using online discourse on the 2024 Street Animal Law in Türkiye as a case study, we collected a dataset comprising 7,320,574 tweets from 537,994 users. From this corpus, 301 users were selected through a high-information sampling strategy and manually annotated by domain experts using a 10-criterion rubric that yields user-level continuous manipulative participation scores. Evaluation under a unified user-level cross-validation protocol showed that the proposed framework accurately estimates both manipulative participation and user stance, with gradient boosting methods providing the best manipulative participation estimates and BERTurk achieving the highest stance classification performance. External validation on an independently annotated user set demonstrated good generalization performance. The findings support modeling manipulative participation as a continuous construct rather than a binary label, providing a more informative basis for computational analyses of the relationship between manipulative participation and stance in online political discourse.

### [37] [Perturbing Inputs Improves Pretraining Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11598)
*Ziyang Cai,Yihe Dong,Dimitris Papailiopoulos,Shivam Garg*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Knowledge distillation trains a student language model to match a teacher's predictions on the training text. We ask whether learning the teacher's behavior beyond the training text can further improve the student. We investigate this using three input perturbations: additive token noise, blending two documents, and blending neighboring tokens. Specifically, for an early part of pretraining we perturb the inputs and train the student to match the teacher on them, and we spend the rest of the same token budget on ordinary distillation. When pretraining from scratch, the best method improves on standard distillation at both scales we tried, by 0.025 nats at 135M parameters and by 0.020 nats at 0.5B (mean of three seeds). At 135M this is 1.45 times the gain that distillation itself provides over next-token training. We also observe promising downstream transfer: at 0.5B, the best variant improves average zero-shot accuracy by about one percentage point across seven tasks. It also retains its validation-loss advantage after low-bit weight quantization. We also test a data-limited setting in which training data must be reused, and find that the gains persist. Finally, ablations suggest that, for additive noise, perturbing the teacher's inputs contributes most of the gain, while perturbing only the student's inputs yields much less.

### [38] [Language model capabilities fail in a shared, predictable order under compression and perturbation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11695)
*Zhixiang Wang,Ulas Bagci*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Compression can preserve a language model's average accuracy while selectively degrading individual capabilities. Whether these losses follow method-specific patterns or a transferable order is unclear. We applied seven perturbation and compression methods to eight instruction-tuned models, scoring 16 tasks in four answer formats against preregistered predictions. Short-answer capabilities failed in nearly the same order under four random perturbations with different mechanisms (median correlation 0.90) and, within each model, under pruning and quantization (0.875). Intact answer margin, answer frequency and answer format predicted this order. Fragility profiles measured under random perturbation predicted which tasks and facts compression removes first and, after four-task calibration, held-out task accuracy (median absolute error 0.11-0.12, against 0.20-0.21 for uniform decline); profiles borrowed from other model families did almost as well. The order did not transfer across models under GPTQ quantization or hold for long-form tasks. Within short answers, what compression removes is predictable before deployment.

### [39] [Explaining and interrupting collective misalignment in language model systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11724)
*Edoardo Chidichimo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: In collectives, language model agents can exchange individually innocuous messages that together support a policy violation. Understanding and preventing collective misalignment requires answering the question of which messages sufficiently influenced and necessarily enabled the violation. Collective Dependence Analysis (CDA) operationalises necessity and sufficiency to explain decisions and find the fewest removals interrupting support within tested combinations. Tests covered constructed violations, unscripted agent conversations, and recorded interactions, with selected message removals reducing violations from 93% to 6% in controlled cases. Using O(N) model evaluations for N messages, CDA achieves the same violation reduction with half the deletions of a frontier LLM judge given the transcript and asked for all supporting messages in eligible operational cases. CDA also proposes the mechanism through which the collective misalignment emerged. Nonetheless, complete explanations remain difficult on unfamiliar tasks and some removals can inadvertently disrupt correct decisions. CDA unifies explanations of collective misalignment with experimentally tested interventions.

### [40] [HiddenPathQA: A Benchmark for Knowledge Graph Question Answering When Questions Hide Their Paths](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11802)
*Sumin Jo,Edward Choi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) systems are typically evaluated on questions whose surface tokens lexically expose the gold KG path. Users, however, may ask questions without knowing the underlying schema: "Which condition could Andrew have due to family history?" compresses a 4-hop chain "Andrew --[father]--> parent --[father]--> grandparent --[medical condition]--> disease --[subclass of]--> hereditary disorder" into a single phrase (family history) that names none of those relations. We identify this collapse of path-question alignment as a blind spot in existing KGQA evaluation. Three major LLM-KG paradigms, hop-by-hop exploration, plan-then-retrieve, and similarity-based retrieval, implicitly rely on such lexical cues, an assumption rarely tested in practice. We make three contributions. (i) We introduce HiddenPathQA, a manually verified benchmark of 1,055 questions spanning 2-6 hops and multiple domains, constructed so that question wording does not reveal the gold path's relations. (ii) We propose Holistic Path Selection, which compares questions against candidate relation chains in the local subgraph as complete units, replacing irreversible per-hop relation scoring with globally informed chain-level reasoning. We develop two implementations, TieredHolistic and FlatHolistic. (iii) We conduct a pseudoword stress test that replaces entity names with meaningless placeholders to distinguish KG-grounded reasoning from entity-level memorization. Holistic Path Selection outperforms six strong KGQA baselines (ToG, PoG, FiDeLiS, R2-KG, KAPING, and KARPA) by 8.8-17.9 accuracy points across two LLM backbones and both original and pseudoword settings. Its advantage under pseudoword replacement shows that the gains cannot be explained by entity-level memorization alone.

### [41] [A Large-Scale Dataset for Cross-Lingual Multi-Jurisdiction Patent Drafting from Patent Cooperation Treaty Applications](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11891)
*Trung Phuong Le,Hirofumi Nonaka,Koji Marusaki,Katsuhito Sudoh,Seiya Kawano*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Securing patent protection across countries requires drafting claims separately for each national patent office, in the relevant language and according to its legal and stylistic conventions. Patent claims can therefore differ across languages and jurisdictions because of translation, target-office drafting practices, and prosecution-stage changes. We formulate cross-lingual patent drafting as generating plausible candidate claim sets for a specified target language, jurisdiction, and prosecution stage from a source claim set in another language. The task models jurisdiction- and stage-specific transformations beyond content-preserving translation. We construct a large-scale Japanese-English dataset by linking Japan Patent Office (JPO) and United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) records through 884,179 Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)-derived patent families. Across six released configurations, these families yield 4,067,168 directional claim-set instances; four core configurations form the main benchmark. Commercial machine translation and zero- and few-shot prompting capture part of the task, while supervised adaptation provides the strongest overall baseline, showing that task-specific patterns can be learned from linked cross-jurisdictional claim sets.

### [42] [BharatSynthQA: A Context-Grounded Question Answering Dataset on Indian Temples and Religious Heritage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11952)
*Riya Naik,Shivam Sharma,Swati Agarwal*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: India's temples and other places of worship are among its richest repositories of cultural heritage, bringing together religious tradition, history, architecture, and art. Due to the widespread curiosity, people increasingly turn to Artificial Intelligence (AI) assistants for information about them. Current models are rarely trained or evaluated on this domain. We present BharatSynthQA, a passage grounded question answering (QA) dataset focused on Indian temples, which also covers other religious sites connected to them. Our pipeline crawls Wikipedia from topics seeded by authentic heritage sources, filters articles for topical relevance, and locations in India. Further it generates Boolean, factoid, and explanatory QA pairs with a fewshot prompted LLM. An LLM judge filters the pairs on answer correctness, retaining 98,677 of 131,494 generated pairs. Additionally, 300 human-annotated pairs are released separately as a reference set. Human evaluation of the subsample of this dataset showed 89.83% of the questions were formed correctly. Benchmarking five current LLMs shows that factoid token F1 is only 0.18-0.30 without the source passage but 0.73-0.77 with it, indicating that this domain is poorly captured in model knowledge. The dataset is available at this https URL to support research on culturally grounded QA and retrieval-augmented generation for Indian heritage.

### [43] [EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11994)
*Fenghai Li,Bingxuan Li,Jiawen Zhang,Yifan Shen,Jiateng Liu,Yutong Zhang,Yue Guo*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Small multimodal models can misjudge emotion when words, voice, and visual cues conflict. We present EmoHarness, which runs such a model, the frozen student, inside a harness: the prompts, settings, and verification code around its calls. A human-written starting harness, the scaffold, numbers the student's visual observations, transcript, and prosody descriptions as citable evidence and has the student weigh candidate emotions against it. In Meta-Harness Evolving (MHE), a stronger LLM, the Builder, reads the student's errors and execution traces offline and edits the harness; static checks and validation gates decide which edits are kept, and the Builder never sees evaluation items. On 5,507 MME-Emotion items, EmoHarness raises task-macro Recognition by 7.6-13.4 points over a single video-only call for all four students and both Builders. Transcripts and prosody descriptions supply most of this boost (+5.38 to +10.71); the scaffold changes the audio-augmented call by -0.79 to +2.54, partly through extra multi-label predictions, and evolved edits add at most +0.95, although no evolved increment survives Holm correction. The harness's emotion context also transfers to IntentQA, with small gains for three of four students, none of which survives correction. EmoHarness thus boosts small multimodal students chiefly by supplying and organizing audio-derived evidence.

### [44] [Lost in Rounding: bf16 Recurrent State Makes Hybrid Reasoning Models Think Longer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12127)
*Yuchuan Weng,Xin Chen,Chi Liu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Hybrid reasoning models interleave attention with recurrent mixers such as Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet, whose state is cached between decoding steps. Prior work showed that storing this state in FP16 or INT8 with round-to-nearest (RTN) makes Mamba-2 and GDN hybrids more verbose, and that stochastic rounding (SR) fixes it. We study the other 16-bit format that serving engines expose, bf16, on six open hybrid reasoning models and 590 competition-math problems. With bf16 RTN state, five of six models reason longer (geometric-mean length 1.07x to 1.27x; also under greedy decoding in the two models tested) and hit the 32K token cap more often. On Qwen3.5-9B, cap hits rise from 118 to 223 and accuracy falls from 85.6% to 70.8%. On LiveCodeBench, both models tested also reason longer and lose 12.6 and 13.4 points of pass@1. Rerunning the capped items with a 128K budget halves the accuracy gap but does not close it (93.6% vs. 86.6%): bf16 runs that never finish are twice as common, and 85% of them are exact repetition loops. On Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2, by contrast, 30 of 31 extra caps finish at 128K, so the cost there is mostly extra tokens (exploratory). Same-width bf16 SR removes the length increase in four of five affected models, restores Qwen3.5-9B to 87.6% and brings code length and pass@1 near FP32 levels, so the failure is mostly rounding bias, not missing resolution. With an integer-hash random generator, SR on Qwen3.5-9B matches FP32 on cap hits and accuracy (113 vs. 118; 85.6% for both) at the memory and decoding speed of bf16 RTN. In the Nemotron-Nano-v2 lineage, SR on 25% of heads (an intermediate-decay band) removes the effect, while random heads and the top teacher-forced-KL octiles do not; in Nemotron-3 and Qwen3.5-9B the effect is spread across heads. We recommend that evaluations of hybrid models report the state dtype, cap rate and output length alongside accuracy.

### [45] [TrajLift: Lifting Memory Recall Trajectories with Latency-Modulated Heat Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12197)
*Jiawen Kang,Jinchao Li,Mingyu Cui,Junan Li,Xixin Wu,Helen Meng*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Verbal memory retrieval carries rich diagnostic information for Alzheimer's disease through the order, hesitation, and categorical organization of recalled words, yet computational modeling of this retrieval process remains largely unexplored. A key challenge is that timing and hierarchical structure are diagnostically entangled: the diagnostic meaning of retrieval timing depends on its hierarchical context. We propose TrajLift, a spectral framework that models verbal recall as timed trajectories on a hierarchical graph. Our central mechanism is latency-modulated heat diffusion on the semantic hierarchy, a unified operator that lifts each recalled word into a representation of both multi-scale hierarchical structure and continuous retrieval timing. Formal analysis shows that the resulting representation is first-order separable into structural and temporal components with spectral selectivity across hierarchical levels. On synthetic benchmarks requiring structure-time interaction, TrajLift stays near-perfect on deep hierarchies where all baselines fail. On real-world clinical data, we show that TrajLift outperforms diverse baselines by jointly modeling timing and semantic structure, with gains that grow as retrieval timing becomes more informative.

### [46] [Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12464)
*Madhusudhana Naidu*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is one target token, and the tokenizer makes that unit look like a constant. It is not. BPE's pretokenizer splits on whitespace before merges are learned, so no multi-word string can ever become a single token: in Qwen3-4B, "United States of America" is four tokens and no adjacent pair of them exists as one entry, so a phrase is out of reach of any method drafting in the target's vocabulary. We change the unit. A small MLP head reads the frozen target's hidden state and predicts a one- to three-word phrase as one entry in a separate draft vocabulary; greedy longest-match expansion maps it back into the target's own tokens, and N candidates are verified in one forward pass behind a prefix-tree mask, so the change is orthogonal to tree depth and width. The target and its tokenizer stay frozen and a candidate is accepted only while it matches the target's own argmax, so the served output is identical to greedy decoding up to floating-point tie-breaking. On one A5000 at batch 1, against HuggingFace generate(), a 21.94M head (0.545% of Qwen3-4B) reaches 2.391x on GSM8K, 2.444x on MATH-500 and 1.544x on MT-Bench. Because the head's output layer is one row of 257 parameters per entry, the draft vocabulary size is the parameter budget: an 8,000-entry head is 3.434M parameters, 0.0854% of the target and 64x smaller than EAGLE-3's drafter, and keeps 92.3% of the larger head's GSM8K tokens per pass. With EAGLE-3 run on same prompts and baseline, our 21.94M head is ahead of tree-16 on both maths sets and behind tree-60 on every set.

Abstract: Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is one target token, and the tokenizer makes that unit look like a constant. It is not. BPE's pretokenizer splits on whitespace before merges are learned, so no multi-word string can ever become a single token: in Qwen3-4B, "United States of America" is four tokens and no adjacent pair of them exists as one entry, so a phrase is out of reach of any method drafting in the target's vocabulary. We change the unit. A small MLP head reads the frozen target's hidden state and predicts a one- to three-word phrase as one entry in a separate draft vocabulary; greedy longest-match expansion maps it back into the target's own tokens, and N candidates are verified in one forward pass behind a prefix-tree mask, so the change is orthogonal to tree depth and width. The target and its tokenizer stay frozen and a candidate is accepted only while it matches the target's own argmax, so the served output is identical to greedy decoding up to floating-point tie-breaking. On one A5000 at batch 1, against HuggingFace generate(), a 21.94M head (0.545% of Qwen3-4B) reaches 2.391x on GSM8K, 2.444x on MATH-500 and 1.544x on MT-Bench. Because the head's output layer is one row of 257 parameters per entry, the draft vocabulary size is the parameter budget: an 8,000-entry head is 3.434M parameters, 0.0854% of the target and 64x smaller than EAGLE-3's drafter, and keeps 92.3% of the larger head's GSM8K tokens per pass. With EAGLE-3 run on same prompts and baseline, our 21.94M head is ahead of tree-16 on both maths sets and behind tree-60 on every set.

</details>


### [47] [Text Grouping Changes Completion-Time Comparisons in Long-Form Simultaneous Speech Translation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12501)
*Hieu Minh Truong,Dung D. Le*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Does grouping translation updates before speech synthesis change the measured completion gap between two translators? We compare StreamAtt with its fixed-audio-history baseline on ten English-German talks. For each translation, we keep the intended text and its availability times fixed and vary how updates are grouped for synthesis. Four-second grouping increases StreamAtt's mean completion lead from 106.6 to 229.1 seconds with XTTS-v2, but reduces it from 169.5 to 146.5 seconds with Piper. Both produce shorter audio; different changes in playback idle account for the opposite effects. These directions recur on a separately selected twenty-talk panel. In continuing CosyVoice 3 sessions, grouping instead leaves paired audio unchanged and delays completion on nineteen of twenty blocks. A speech-timing comparison therefore needs to specify how text enters synthesis, not just which synthesizer is used. Recognition and automatic word timing describe the outputs, but do not establish translation accuracy or intelligibility.

### [48] [AgentOPSD: Turn-Level Credit Assignment via Recursive Belief Revision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12587)
*Yizhuo Li*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards ordinarily spreads a single advantage over a whole trajectory, a granularity too coarse to isolate the few decisions on which success in a long, multi-turn interaction actually turns. Privileged self-distillation supplies denser supervision, but it leaves unanswered how a set of local teacher-student discrepancies should be converted into credit along a sequence. We introduce AgentOPSD, a critic-free scheme that assigns credit recursively, one interaction turn at a time. Inside a turn, the token-level log-probability gaps between a skill-conditioned self-teacher and the student are summed, and that sum acts as evidence in a recursive Bayesian update carried out in log-odds space; the resulting revisions reallocate the outcome-derived advantage across turns through a multiplier that is bounded and preserves its sign. With Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B as policy backbones on ALFWorld, the method improves consistently on GRPO and on self-distillation baselines, and attains 89.1% success at the 7B scale. Ablations attribute the gain to aggregating evidence at turn boundaries and to making the belief revision depend on history, rather than to the local gap by itself.

### [49] [Unmasking Four Knapsack Problems in the Traveling Thief Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12597)
*Mohammed Mizan Alanazi,Mahdi Khemakhem*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: The traveling thief problem (TTP) asks a thief to choose a tour and a packing together, and the benchmark of 9,720 instances of Polyakovskiy et al. (2014) is the standard test set for comparing TTP heuristics. We show that four of these instances are not TTP instances at all. Their files give a renting rate of 0.00, so the tour has no effect on the objective and each instance reduces to a 0-1 knapsack problem. One of them belongs to the 60 categorized instances on which new methods are usually compared, and on it five of nine published methods report exactly the same value. The cause is the format of the files, which keep the renting rate with two decimals, while the rule of the generator gives a rate close to 0.003 on these instances. The same rounding may shift the rate of 949 other instances by more than 1%. Since the tour and the packing used by the generator were not published, the original rates cannot be recovered. We therefore define new rates with the same rule, applied to a fully specified reference solution that we publish, and we show with a published heuristic that the corrected instances behave as TTP instances again. We also give reference results on the corrected instances and recommendations for future studies. Finally, we present ttplib, a new open-source Python library that loads any of the 9,720 instances, including the corrected ones, without downloading the whole benchmark.

### [50] [Adapting Small Language Models to Romanized Nepali: Tokenizer Fertility, Reference Likelihood, and Generation Metrics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12628)
*Pujan Pant,Sagar Newpane,Hari Sitaula,Manish Sakhakarmy*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Romanized Nepali, Nepali written in Latin script, is common in digital communication but has no standard spelling and few resources, and it is unclear how reliably small open language models can be adapted to it. We adapt three 2-3B base models from different families, Llama-3.2-3B, Qwen2.5-3B, and Gemma-2-2B, with QLoRA on 9,000 instruction examples produced by deterministic transliteration of Nepali instruction data. Each model is trained with one shared recipe and three seeds and evaluated on 1,000 held-out examples with reference-overlap metrics, byte-normalized reference likelihood (bits per byte, BPB), and an output audit, against zero-shot baselines under two prompts. Fine-tuning raises chrF++ from 10-14 to 29.0-30.6 and lowers BPB from 2.23-2.41 to 0.78-0.84; most zero-shot outputs (54-92%) are English-like. Likelihood and overlap disagree on how far apart the models are. Llama-3.2-3B has the lowest BPB in every seed, 0.042 below Qwen2.5-3B (95% CI 0.039-0.046), yet the two cannot be separated on chrF++ (30.51 and 30.61) or BLEU, even with paired item-level tests. Gemma-2-2B, whose tokenizer splits Romanized Nepali words least (2.72 tokens per word), scores worst on every measure. Which model gains most over its zero-shot baseline depends on the zero-shot prompt. In a supplementary comparison with an identical tokenizer, Llama-3.1-8B lowers BPB by 0.053 (0.050-0.056) relative to Llama-3.2-3B, while chrF++ and BLEU rise by only 0.68 and 0.58 points. Lower fertility and higher reference likelihood therefore did not identify the model whose outputs were closest to the references.

### [51] [The Narrative Gap: Can LLMs Help Us Navigate Diverse Narratives Across Languages?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12750)
*Nikhil Sharma,Kelly Marchisio,Kenton Murray,Ziang Xiao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly mediate how people seek and consume information, including accounts that differ across languages and regions, especially on contested topics. Supporting diverse information seeking requires models to help users navigate competing narratives across languages and information streams. We define six capabilities necessary for diverse multilingual information seeking: three foundational capabilities for narrative inclusion, narrative exclusion, and missing narrative identification; and three higher-level capabilities for presenting diverse narratives, preserving narrative coverage under confirmatory queries, and maintaining information parity across languages. To guide the development of those information seeking capabilities, we introduce \textsc{NarrativeBench}, a benchmark comprising 1,333 news articles in 23 publication languages across 23 contested topics and 460 Reddit-grounded queries. Evaluating 14 LLMs across 24 query languages, we find that current models lack the capabilities needed to reliably navigate diverse narratives, limiting users' control over the perspectives they receive and leaving substantial gaps in exposure to competing accounts even when diversity is explicitly requested. Information access also differs across query framings and languages, risking echo chambers, linguistic filter bubbles, and information disparities that weaken the common ground needed for democratic discourse. \textsc{NarrativeBench} provides a foundation for developing information systems that give users across languages and regions agency to navigate diverse narratives.

### [52] [PORT: Preference Optimization via Robust Token-Level Reweighting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12763)
*Ding Zhu,Xiukun Wei,Tian Xie,Zhihui Zhu,Xueru Zhang,Mohammad Mahdi Khalili*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Preference optimization has become a central approach for aligning large language models with human values, but its effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of preference annotations. In practice, preference data is often noisy due to annotation errors and ambiguity. Existing robust preference optimization methods primarily operate at the sequence level, implicitly treating entire responses as uniformly correct or incorrect. However, rejected responses may still contain informative reasoning steps, while preferred responses can include subtle errors. In this work, we propose \textbf{P}reference \textbf{O}ptimization via \textbf{R}obust \textbf{T}oken-level reweighting \textbf{(PORT)}, a fine-grained framework for robust alignment under noisy preferences. PORT performs token-level reweighting using the empirical cumulative distribution function (CDF) of token log-probabilities, yielding an efficient forward-pass-only proxy to gradient-norm penalization that selectively suppresses corrupted tokens without additional backward-pass computation. We provide theoretical analysis showing that PORT reduces the gradient bias from noisy preference labels by minimizing an upper bound on the bias term. Extensive experiments across diverse noise settings demonstrate that PORT consistently improves robustness and outperforms existing sequence-level baselines. The code is available at this https URL

### [53] [HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12872)
*Haozhen Zhang,Bohan Liu,Jianzhu Bao,Qingyuan Liu,Haodong Yue,Xiao Li,Zi Pong Lim,Wenya Wang*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: As multimodal agents accumulate increasingly long interaction histories, effectively retrieving and utilizing past information becomes critical for long-term interaction. Existing memory systems typically rely on semantic retrieval over compressed memories and expose predefined representations, which may miss relevant memories and overlook heterogeneous evidence needs across queries. We introduce \textbf{\hivemem}, a multimodal memory framework that interleaves \textbf{\textsc{H}}or\textbf{\textsc{i}}zontal Memory Expansion with \textbf{\textsc{Ve}}rtical Evidence Composition. For horizontal memory expansion, \hivemem organizes memory episodes into a relational graph using textual and visual anchors, expanding semantically retrieved seeds with related neighbors to recover complementary information. For vertical evidence composition, each retrieved memory retains multiple evidence forms, including compact summaries, captions, grounded visual views, raw images, and interaction history. A lightweight trainable selector independently composes an evidence subset for each retrieved memory, enabling query-adaptive utilization of heterogeneous multimodal information. This two-dimensional design jointly broadens memory coverage and adapts the evidence contributed by individual memories. Experiments across three multimodal memory benchmarks show that \hivemem consistently improves task performance across base models while reducing token consumption by about 90\% compared with the most efficient competing multimodal baselines.

### [54] [A local language model layered with rule-based and neural detectors for clinical text de-identification: an open-source toolkit and evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12709)
*Valentin Burkin*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Objectives: To measure whether a locally hosted large language model (LLM), stacked with deterministic and clinical named-entity recognition (NER) detectors, finds more protected health information (PHI) than open tools, and at what precision. Materials and Methods: DeidSharp, an open-source .NET toolkit, combines the findings of pluggable detectors (patterns, a clinical NER model, a local 26B mixture-of-experts LLM) and fails closed on any detector error. Configurations fixed on tuning halves were compared, under a prespecified protocol, with deid, Philter, the Stanford/Penn de-identifier, OpenAI Privacy Filter and GLiNER on reporting halves of PhysioNet's nursing notes (889 spans) and semi-synthetic MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries (29,023 spans), and on synthetic ASQ-PHI queries, with paired patient-level bootstrap intervals. Results: In the nursing notes, against Stanford/Penn, the recall-first stack found 98.9% of PHI (+2.8, 95% CI 1.4 to 4.4) at 9.3 points lower precision; the precision-first stack, without NER, found 96.5%, matching Stanford/Penn, at 19.6 points higher precision (83.2%). In the discharge summaries, both stacks led Stanford/Penn by more than 20 points (recall-first 95.3%, +21.5, 20.5 to 22.4), almost entirely on generated untyped names; on typed labels all three exceeded 99%. All four prespecified comparisons held. No configuration beat deid significantly on its home corpus; Philter found more discharge-summary spans than the recall-first stack at 23 points lower precision. Discussion: The LLM was the main detector and NER added place names; asked to verify its own findings, the LLM discarded a quarter of true PHI. Conclusion: A local LLM layered with deterministic detectors offers recall-first and precision-first operating points without sending text off-site.

### [55] [WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12856)
*Zheng Jiang,Fang Niu,Bo Peng,Houde Qian,Wenyi Li,Deyao Hong,Mingju Gao,Yizhe Chi,Youjie Zheng,Kaisen Yang,Calvin Xiao,Lifeng Sun,Huan-ang Gao*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Large language model agents are increasingly deployed as multi-agent systems rather than as a standalone model operating within a single context. Recent agent harnesses allow the model to instantiate worker agents and to author the executable workflow that coordinates them, shifting the design of system structure from developers to the model at run time. The quality of this organization therefore constitutes a distinct capability, yet existing benchmarks either measure end-to-end task completion or evaluate coordination under structures specified in advance. We formalize this capability as workflow orchestration and introduce WorkflowArena, a benchmark of 145 long-horizon tasks spanning 8 professional domains, from software engineering and formal mathematics to legal analysis and 3D production. Each task specifies an initial workspace and an integrated deliverable composed of interdependent components, which is assessed by a hidden verifier. Agents determine autonomously whether and how to delegate, and all delegation is recorded, enabling joint evaluation of deliverable quality and the organization of the underlying work. Experiments with nine models show that no single configuration performs best across all domains and that systems exhibit distinct delegation strategies: at high effort, Claude models in Claude Code invoke workflows less frequently but with larger worker groups, whereas GPT models in Codex delegate more frequently in smaller units. When the executing model is held fixed on a challenging subset of tasks, workflows authored by Claude Opus 5.5 substantially improve weaker executors, indicating that workflow organization is itself a measurable determinant of task performance.

### [56] [Rethinking Supervision Targets for Multimodal LLM Unlearning: Less Private Information, Reduced Distribution Shift](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09939)
*Leijiang Gu,Zhen Zeng,Feng Li,Le Zhang,Zenglin Shi*

Main category: cs.CL

TL;DR: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can memorize and reproduce sensitive information from their training data, posing significant privacy risks. Their ability to encode knowledge across both textual and visual modalities further complicates the selective removal of such private information. Many existing methods guide model unlearning by training the model toward constructed labels or output distributions, which we refer to as supervision targets. However, these methods often suffer from a trade-off between forgetting effectiveness and model utility. We identify supervision target limitations as a key factor in this trade-off and empirically show that targets containing more private information lead to insufficient forgetting, while larger distribution shifts from the original output distribution are associated with greater utility degradation. Motivated by these findings, we propose FFN-Perturbed Self-Distillation (FPD), which starts from the teacher's original output distribution as a zero-shift reference and selectively perturbs FFN activations associated with private information across textual and visual modalities. By precisely reducing private information from the teacher's original output distribution, FPD constructs supervision targets with less private information and reduced distribution shift. Extensive experiments on S-MLLMUn Bench demonstrate that FPD achieves a better forgetting-utility trade-off than existing methods.
